Thursday, 11:40 p.m.
Coding bootcamp, week fourteen. Today's project was a login page. I sat there for three hours and felt nothing except a dull headache.
Nirmala Bua paid half the fees. I paid the other half from my savings from the bakery job. Six months, gone into this. And at my farewell from the bakery I told everyone, 'I'm going to be a developer.' They clapped. Uncle Baljinder even gave me a keyboard.
So I can't quit now. What would I say? 'Sorry, I was wrong'? Everyone would look at me like that.
The only good part of my day was lunch, when I helped the canteen aunty ice a cake for someone's birthday. My hands knew what to do. I didn't want to go back to the laptop.
I'm annoyed with myself, with the course, with everyone who clapped.
Eight more weeks. I'll finish. I have to.
Gurpreet

You want to drop the engineering course? Sit, sit. Let your Shreya Mausi tell you about my second year of commerce.
At twenty I joined an expensive coaching class for accountancy. Papa had paid a whole year's fees. I'd told all my friends I was going to be a chartered accountant. By the third month I hated it. I'd sit in the back row, doodling, stomach in knots.
But I kept going. Every morning I thought, the fees are paid, everyone knows, if I quit I'm admitting I was wrong. I started resenting Papa, the teacher, even my friends who were happy.
I stayed a full year. Failed the exam anyway. Only then did I switch to design, which I loved.
That year wasn't a waste because I stayed. It was a waste because I stayed for the wrong reasons.
